newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodia lures investment to broaden tax base.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia lures investment to broaden tax base.

text.p: The projected $500 million in foreign investment Cambodia expects in 1996 may help broaden its critically small tax base, government officials and business leaders said this week.

Vichit Ith, secretary general of the Cambodian Investment Board (CIB), told Reuters in an interview this week that about 35 percent of the $500 million in projects would be implemented by the end of the year.
Foreign investment in Cambodia has been on the rise since the formation of the CIB in 1994.
Vuthy Chea, director of the CIB's information division, said without elaborating that this year's projected $500 million in investment was a "slight increase over 1995."
Taiwan is the largest foreign investor in Cambodia this year followed by China. Industry is the leading sector so far, with $124 million in projects approved this year.
The 1996 investment will be crucial to reducing Cambodia's dependence on customs duties, which make up nearly half of the country's revenue, analysts said.
"With overseas investment, we can reduce our reliance on (the customs tax) and imports," said Kong Triv, a leader in the Phnom Penh Chamber of Commerce and president of KT Pacific Group Ltd.

Finance Minister Keat Chhon has said that unless a broader tax base is formed, Cambodia will be hit hard when it harmonises its customs regime with members of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) under the ASEAN Free Trade Agreement.
Cambodia has observer status in ASEAN and will achieve full membership in July 1997. ASEAN groups Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam.
No one expects ASEAN will let Cambodia collapse, even if the country fails to lure more investment.
"We will have to attempt to keep pace with the rest of the region," said Kao Kim Hourn, exective director of the Cambodian Institute for Cooperation and Peace.
